Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. When Melissa joined Kyle Denton and me on InnerVerse, we explored the premise that spirit precedes form, and homeopathy demonstrates that principle as plainly as anything I know. RMDY makes quality remedies and first aid kits accessible, prepared with real care for who makes the medicine and how.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Divination as a Conversation With Yourself", "body": "Chance sets divination apart from fortune telling, calling it a conversation with yourself, and says whatever he is egoically stuck on never stops turning up in the cards. Rachel describes her practice as a visual conversation with the divine that leads her down pathways she might not have thought of. A second guest from the Telegram group says her morning rune pulls show the theme of the day and what she is not looking at, and that ego or fear driven questions get a different answer than the one asked."}, {"title": "Runes as Glyphs of Nature and Wealth", "body": "Rachel sees the runes as glyphs that grew out of pictographs, patterns of nature that describe growth the way Chance's I Ching hexagrams do. She lays out the Elder Futhark as three sets of eight and opens with a pair of cattle runes: Fehu, the herd you own and work with symbiotically, and Uruz, the wild ox, the free abundance of nature, like the wild kale in her yard. She links those runes to tarot pentacles and Taurus, and shows the set she made herself from bottle caps instead of wood."}, {"title": "A Spiral Hero's Journey Up Yggdrasil", "body": "Asked about a hero's journey, Rachel reads each set of eight as a stage up the world tree Yggdrasil: arrival on earth, Raidho the horse and the journey, a gift that comes with a sacrifice such as an old belief, and finally joy. The three sets move from the foundation of being, to time and cycles, to stepping into your own divinity. She calls it a spiral rather than a circle, since no fall is ever the same fall, and Chance ties it to eternal return and the paradox of freeing your will into the cosmic will."}, {"title": "Isa, Ice and the Present Moment", "body": "Rachel names Isa, the ice rune, as a favourite and draws on the Havamal, attributed to Odin, where ice sits among the things you cannot trust. In her reading ice is the now moment, with only an illusion of stability, so she treats it as a lesson in healthy non-attachment and being okay with mistakes. She places the past with Hel, Loki's daughter, the underworld of ancestors and memory, and describes the whole Norse cosmology as a balance of fire and ice. Chance adds that the present is a narrow band between the two."}, {"title": "Odin, Peter Pan and Growing Up", "body": "Chance says so many people tell him Odin or Hermes visits their dreams that he wonders whether the figure is a mature higher self. Rachel sees such gods as ancient ancestors, says the father archetype is surfacing as an era shifts, and cautions against treating Odin and Hermes as one entity, a point Chance concedes. Chance then reads Peter Pan, since pan means all, as an inverted All Father stuck in eternal childhood, and Rachel adds wolf cults of Odin and the Aries challenge of keeping an inner child alive."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Rachel M is an active member of the InnerVerse telegram group who is involved with divinatory arts like tarot and rune-reading. In this live stream, we'll be introducing the use of the Futhark runes while tangentially touching on other tarot-type topics, and exploring Odin, I Ching, Gene Keys, and more.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Hour 2 of this podcast is reserved for Rokfin & Patreon members.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Fate, destiny and free will in the Odin myth", "body": "Chance Garton asks whether Odin, who knows the wolf Fenrir is destined to slay him, shows that we can know our own fate. Rachel Munoz answers with a framework she draws from Druidry: fate is what you arrive with, your patterns and inheritance, destiny is your potential, and will sits between them. In her reading, Odin's fixation on his ending blinded him to his fullest potential, much as an anxious ego rehearses worst cases it can never truly predict. She sees Fenrir as primal nature, the return to the deep that no one escapes."}, {"title": "Love, fear and the solar plexus", "body": "Chance Garton offers his view that fear is the conviction that only one outcome is possible, while love sees many possibilities and needs no particular result. He links this to a constriction he works on in his own solar plexus with sound therapy, and cites Eileen Day McKusick's advice to live from the solar plexus more than the heart. Rachel Munoz connects the idea to author Richard Rudd, who describes the solar plexus as a second brain, and she frames it as a filter between the heart and the creative center that shapes what a person ends up making."}, {"title": "Gene Keys as a path from shadow to gift", "body": "Rachel Munoz introduces the Gene Keys as a synthesis built on the 64 I Ching hexagrams and related to human design, calculated from a birth time. She describes it as a tool for transmuting shadows, which she says come from ego, fear and survival but are not inherently evil. She holds that the work operates on an epigenetic level, a claim she presents as her understanding. Chance Garton walks through Gene Key 48, from inadequacy to resourcefulness to wisdom, and Gene Key 25, which he relates to constriction, grief held in the lungs and a return to acceptance."}, {"title": "Balance over hierarchy between light and dark", "body": "Using the rune Dagaz, whose shape echoes the infinity symbol, Rachel Munoz argues that relationships are not meant to be stacked with one side above the other, and she links rigid hierarchy to a Gene Keys shadow and to episodes like the witch burnings. Through Eihwaz, the yew tree rune, she describes trees as conduits that balance the light and the dark naturally. Chance Garton adds his opinion that the real distortion is not light or dark itself but the urge to label one side bad and override its free will, which he ties to the trickster nature of Odin."}, {"title": "Letting divination live in everyday life", "body": "Rachel Munoz says apps can deliver messages but feel too etheric, while handling physical runes makes a reading more personal and meaningful. Chance Garton agrees that ceremony sharpens his own readings. After a live draw of Berkano and Perthro alongside his I Ching cast of hexagram 49, revolution, changing to 33, retreat, the two discuss walking away from patterns that no longer serve. Rachel says she does not read for herself every day, preferring to let practice show up on its own, such as runes appearing in sticks, roots and branches on a hike, and urges people to see life as an art form."}]
